summary: Nebraska is unusually clear: its statute defining 'wild mammals' (Neb. Rev. Stat. 37-246) EXCLUDES 'the black rat' by name (alongside the house mouse, Norway rat, fallow deer, and feral dogs/cats). 'Black rat' is the common name for Rattus rattus. Because the Captive Wildlife Permit system and the prohibited-species list (wolf/skunk/cats/bears) are scoped to 'wild mammals,' the roof rat falls entirely outside them — so keeping, breeding, and selling/giving is legal at the state level with no permit. The one procedural requirement is interstate IMPORT: the Dept of Agriculture lists rats among pet rodents needing a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection + an import permit. (Statute uses the common name, so a written Game & Parks confirmation is the only loose end.)

keep.why: Neb. Rev. Stat. 37-246 defines 'wild mammals' but EXCLUDES 'the black rat' (= Rattus rattus) by name. The Captive Wildlife Permit requirement (37-477) applies only to wild mammals/birds/nongame wildlife, and the prohibited list (37-479: wolf, skunk, Felidae, Ursidae) doesn't include rats — so no state permit is required to keep one.
keep.governing_law: Neb. Rev. Stat. 37-246 (excludes 'the black rat'); 37-477 (permit trigger); 37-479 (prohibited species).

breed.why: The captive-wildlife propagation permits (37-477/37-480) reach only 'wild mammals' as defined; R. rattus is excluded, so breeding needs no permit. The Commercial Dog and Cat Act covers only dogs/cats. Hobby breeding is unregulated by the state.
breed.governing_law: Neb. Rev. Stat. 37-246; 37-477, 37-480; 54-625 et seq. (dogs/cats only).

sell_give.why: The captive-wildlife sale/barter rules (37-480) apply only to 'wild mammals'; R. rattus is excluded, and no Nebraska pet-dealer license covers non-livestock rodents (the Commercial Dog and Cat Act is dogs/cats). Within-state gifting and small sales are unregulated; commercial scale may trigger federal USDA/AWA licensing.

transport.why: Within-state transport of a lawfully-owned pet is unregulated. For IMPORT, the Dept of Agriculture (Neb. Admin. Code Title 23 ch. 21) requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (within 30 days) + an import permit, and explicitly lists rats among the pet rodents covered. Confirm the single-pet process with the State Veterinarian. Never release a roof rat.
transport.governing_law: Neb. Admin. Code Title 23 ch. 21 §004 (import CVI + permit; rats listed); NDA Summary of Import Requirements.

restrictions.summary: Importing a pet rat into Nebraska requires a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection (within 30 days) + an import permit from the State Veterinarian (NDA lists rats among covered pet rodents). No CVI for in-state movement; never release.
restrictions.where_to_file: Nebraska Dept of Agriculture, State Veterinarian

restrictions.summary: Local (Lincoln/Omaha/county) ordinances may separately regulate rats — check your city. Never release a roof rat.
